dedupe_keys.name: adaptation strategy and action plan for wetlands of the attica region under drought greece

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the adaptation strategy and action plan for the more than 100 wetlands of the Attica Region in Greece, including streams, estuaries, coastal marshes and lagoons, lakes and artificial wetlands, which suffer from increasing drought and pressure from a dense population and competing land uses. The strategy, prepared in the OrientGate project from 2012 to 2014, has seven axes, each with prioritised measures in the Attica Wetland Action Plan, centred on preserving and restoring wetlands, improving their ecological connectivity as green infrastructure and securing legal designation and adaptive management. The first stage of implementation ran from 2015 to 2020 and continues under the regional adaptation plan and the 2021 to 2027 operational programme, coordinated by the region's Environment Directorate. Expected benefits include coastal protection, water quality, flood and drought buffering and habitat. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2023), citing the action plan and Hatziiordanou and others (2019). Caveats: benefits are expected, not measured, and implementation depends on regional funding. It illustrates regional adaptation planning for blue infrastructure under drought; a related record is the Ecosystem Services Valuation Database.
name: Adaptation strategy and action plan for wetlands of the Attica Region under drought (Greece)
outcomes: A regional strategy and action plan for over 100 wetlands was adopted and implemented in a first stage from 2015 to 2020, continuing under the regional adaptation plan.
